title: Polynomial equations with a unit Jacobian minor near a regular closed point
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], S a finite type k-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and m a maximal ideal such that S_m is regular local [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-regular-scheme]. There exist g in S outside m, natural numbers n,c, polynomials f_j in k[y_1,...,y_n] indexed by j in Fin c [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], a k-algebra isomorphism e: k[y_1,...,y_n]/(f_j) -> S_g [def-weil-ring-localization-away], and a strictly increasing map i: Fin c -> Fin n, such that the quotient image of det(partial f_j/partial y_(i(l)))_(j,l) is a unit [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant, def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]. This asserts a specified algebraic presentation and an invertible minor; smoothness is not a premise or conclusion.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00TS, implication (1) => (4), polynomial-presentation and conormal-rank argument; Lemma 00TE, converse inverse-variable construction

proof.text: Install maximality and regularity as local instances. Apply the independently proved source regular-closed-point theorem Algebra.IsSmoothAt.of_isRegularLocalRing_of_isAlgClosed. Since k is Noetherian, finite type implies finite presentation. Apply Mathlib Algebra.IsSmoothAt.exists_notMem_isStandardSmooth to obtain g outside m and a standard smooth presentation of S_g.

Unpack IsStandardSmooth.out into finite index types and a submersive presentation P. Reindex its variables by Fin n. Lift the linear order of Fin n to the relation indices along the injective variable selection, then use monoEquivOfFin to enumerate them increasingly. Reindex the relations by this order isomorphism. SubmersivePresentation.reindex preserves the unit Jacobian; by the lifted order the resulting map Fin c -> Fin n is strictly increasing. These constructions work for c=0 and n=0.

Use Presentation.quotientEquiv.restrictScalars k as the required algebra equivalence; span_range_relation_eq_ker identifies its domain. Transport jacobian_isUnit backwards along this equivalence using MulEquiv.isUnit_map. The matrix in the statement is the transpose of PreSubmersivePresentation.jacobiMatrix by jacobiMatrix_apply, so Matrix.det_transpose identifies its determinant with the unit just obtained. No arbitrary unproved witness or additional equation is introduced.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_jacobian_unit_presentation_of_regularAtMaximal
    (k : Type u) (S : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    [IsAlgClosed k] [Algebra.FiniteType k S]
    (m : Ideal S) (hm : m.IsMaximal)
    (hreg : IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime m)) :
    ∃ (g : S), g ∉ m ∧
      ∃ (n c : ℕ) (f : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)
        (e : (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)) ≃ₐ[k]
          Localization.Away g) (i : Fin c → Fin n),
        StrictMono i ∧ IsUnit (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range f))
          (Matrix.det (fun j l : Fin c ↦ MvPolynomial.pderiv (i l) (f j))))
